newsitem.title: SPAIN: Peseta debt/interbank market closing report.
newsitem.headline: Peseta debt/interbank market closing report.

text.p: Spain's long bond future closed at a record high, erasing earlier losses after strong performances in world bond markets, dealers said.
"We are mainly pulled higher by foreign markets with no domestic news in sight," a Madrid-based dealer said.
Earlier, the announcement of a modest rise in U.S. payrolls made a Federal Reserve rate hike look less likely.
Chart experts see very strong resistance at around 117.75/80 while the new support is at 117.17.
The 10-year spread over bunds fell slightly to around 67 basis points from 68 basis points at the open. But dealers ruled out a bigger change in the spread in the near term.
"It's unlikely the spread will move from here," a dealer said. The Bank of Spain's decision to hold its 5.25 percent official rate was widely discounted and did not affect prices, dealers added.
But they also reported a flattening in the yield curve.
"Nobody has buying interest in the five-year bonds. With the long end climbing higher, the effect is a global flattening of the yield curve," a dealer explained.
The market consensus now suggests the Bank of Spain could hold its monetary policy steady until the end of August or beginning of September.
